 South Korea to rebuild Washington embassy for first time in 70 years at estimated cost of W300b
 by 
 Yang Dae-geun 
Published : Nov. 16, 2026 - 16:00:48
 Copy Completed! 
 View Korean Original
 South Korean Ambassador to the United States Kang Kyung-wha (left) and Cultural Heritage Administration chief Heo Min speak at the consular building of the South Korean Embassy in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 9 (local time), after a commemorative bronze plaque marking the building as South Korea's first embassy was installed under the Cultural Heritage Administration's initiative. [Yonhap] South Korea is pushing to fully reconstruct its embassy building in Washington, D.C. The chancery, completed in 1954, is considered a symbol of South Korea-US diplomatic relations.
 According to the office of People Power Party lawmaker Kim Dae-sik of the National Assembly's Foreign Affairs and Unification Committee, the committee's budget subcommittee is currently discussing whether to add a South Korean Embassy chancery reconstruction project as a new item under the overseas mission facility maintenance and management category in next year's general account budget.
 The project cost is estimated at around 270 billion won ($202 million), with an additional 30 billion won projected for renting a temporary building during construction, bringing the total provisional estimate to 300 billion won.
 Both ruling and opposition parties agree that the current building is severely lacking in workspace, event facilities, parking and staff welfare areas needed to carry out the full range of diplomatic functions expected of an overseas mission. The embassy issued a public notice in 2024 for a basic reconstruction concept and feasibility review study.
 However, some observers say the reconstruction is unlikely to be reflected in next year's budget right away. A large-scale reconstruction — as opposed to routine facility maintenance — must draw funding from the state property management fund rather than the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' general account budget.
 Under the fund's operating guidelines, buildings completed more than 15 years ago may be considered for remodeling, with a review process determining whether the project is included in the fund's operating plan. The Foreign Affairs and Unification Committee is scheduled to hold its budget subcommittee sessions at the National Assembly on Tuesday and Wednesday.
